author.name: Susan B. Anthony
author.heading: About Susan B. Anthony
author.bio: Susan B. Anthony was a reformer whose work centered on women’s voting rights. She collaborated with Elizabeth Cady Stanton in organizing, publishing and campaigning, and also worked in the abolitionist movement. Her arguments linked political representation with women’s economic and personal independence.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: The sentence frames equality as participation in making law, rather than protection granted by others. Stanford’s quotation page preserves Anthony’s name but supplies no original occasion, and the museum teaching resource repeats the attribution. The related historical speech PDF could not be accessed, so it is not used to reconstruct a speech context. Stanford quotation page ↗
